title: requireScope substring-matches when a key document stores scopes as a STRING: scopes "calendar:read" passes requireScope("calendar") because String.prototype.includes is used, not Array
area: apps/api/src/auth.ts requireScope; apps/api/src/store.ts verify (line 47, scopes: doc.scopes ?? [] is not validated as an array)
evidence: node --import tsx probe: requireScope("calendar")({auth:{tenantId:"t",scopes:"calendar:read"}}, res, next) calls next (1 call). Not reachable with a schema-valid key (VerifiedKey.scopes is string[]), only with a corrupted/legacy key document whose scopes field is a string; null/object/number scopes throw TypeError instead (refused, 500 path). No test asserts the wrong behaviour; require-scope.test.ts pins only string values that do NOT contain the scope.
fix_direction: In requireScope use Array.isArray(req.auth.scopes) && includes; and/or validate scopes in store.verify (non-array -> treat as [] or reject the key). Add a require-scope.test.ts case: string scopes "calendar:read" vs "calendar" => 403.
